findings.evidence: `Ideal.lean:227` `mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters {f u} (hf : f ∈ virtualCharacters k G) (hu : u ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P) : f * u ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`; the PR itself derives the strong form from the weak one at `Artin.lean:235-239`: `simpa [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters hf (natCard_nsmul_one_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic ...)`.
findings.fix: Move the `Rational scalar extension` section below `mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters` and replace the hypothesis with `h : n • (1 : G → k) ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`, recovering the general case internally by `simpa [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using mul_mem_indVirtualCharacters hf h`. The two call sites in `Artin.lean` then pass `natCard_nsmul_one_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` directly (and, for the elementary case, its image under `indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic_le_indVirtualCharacters_isElementary`).
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacterDirectSumBaseChangeRat_surjective` assumes `∀ f ∈ virtualCharacters k G, n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`, but the ideal property in the same file makes the single membership `n • (1 : G → k) ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P` equivalent and sufficient; the advertised "general criterion" is therefore harder to apply than it needs to be, and is inconsistent with its own n = 1 analogue `indVirtualCharacters_eq_virtualCharacters_iff` (line 246), which is stated in the minimal `1 ∈ V_G` form.

summary: The sharp Artin results are at the right level (arbitrary field, no algebraic-closure or invertibility hypotheses) and the family generalization of `indCharacterSpanInt` matches the existing `indCharacterSpan` design. The one defect is the rational-surjectivity criterion, whose hypothesis is stronger than the single membership it needs.
